⚠️ Security-sensitive changes

This PR adds SHA-256 content hashing to epoch snapshots to detect and drop re-wrapped commit events that carry identical ciphertext, preventing replayed outer wrappers from winning MIP-03 commit ordering and causing unnecessary rollbacks and client desynchronization. It records a content hash for applied commits and uses it in the better-candidate check to reject candidates with identical ciphertext while still converging snapshot anchor metadata to a canonical MIP-03 winner among wrappers.

**What changed**:
- EpochSnapshot now includes applied_commit_content_hash: [u8; 32] to store a SHA-256 digest of the outer event content (base64(nonce || ciphertext)).  
- EpochSnapshotManager::create_snapshot(...) and ::is_better_candidate(...) signatures were extended to accept a content_hash: &[u8; 32] and persist/compare it.  
- is_better_candidate() rejects candidates whose content hash equals the stored applied_commit_content_hash (when known), preventing rollback on re-wrapped identical ciphertext.  
- When a same-ciphertext wrapper is nevertheless the MIP-03 winner, the snapshot’s applied_commit_ts and applied_commit_id are updated to converge on a canonical anchor while still rejecting the candidate for rollback.  
- Snapshot hydration initializes applied_commit_content_hash to [0u8; 32] when the original hash is unavailable (treated as “unknown”).  
- Added pub(crate) content_hash(content: &str) -> [u8; 32] helper (sha2::Sha256) and threaded content-hash computation through commit, pending-commit, and error/rollback code paths.  
- Error::ProcessMessageWrongEpoch was changed to ProcessMessageWrongEpoch(u64, bool) so the recovery path only triggers rollback/`is_better_candidate` for commit messages.

Affected crates: mdk-core.

**Security impact**:
- Adds cryptographic replay detection by storing a SHA-256 hash of outer event content to prevent replay-triggered rollbacks and client desynchronization.  
- No changes to encryption primitives, key derivation, nonce formats, key storage, or HKDF contexts—only a content hash is recorded for deduplication.  
- Hydrated snapshots that lack prior hash use a zeroed hash to represent “unknown prior state,” deferring deduplication until an applied commit records a real hash.

**Protocol changes**:
- Modifies MIP-03 commit ordering handling by introducing ciphertext deduplication: identical-ciphertext re-wrapped events are rejected during the better-candidate check while snapshot anchors converge to the canonical MIP-03 winner among wrappers.

**API surface**:
- Internal breaking changes within mdk-core: EpochSnapshot gains applied_commit_content_hash and EpochSnapshotManager::create_snapshot()/::is_better_candidate() now require content_hash parameters, and Error::ProcessMessageWrongEpoch now includes an is_commit boolean; no UniFFI/FFI, storage schema, or cross-crate public API additions beyond these mdk-core signature/struct changes.

## Summary

Replaces `blurhash` with [`fast-thumbhash`](https://crates.io/crates/fast-thumbhash) — a 12x faster ThumbHash encoder/decoder with built-in base91 encoding. Removes the standalone `base64` dependency.

Since this MDK release already introduces breaking changes, this is the ideal time to migrate the ecosystem from BlurHash to ThumbHash. [Vector](https://github.com/VectorPrivacy/Vector) — an MDK client — has already fully transitioned to ThumbHash in production, and we built `fast-thumbhash` specifically to deliver massive benefits over both traditional BlurHash and the reference ThumbHash libraries: 12x faster encoding/decoding, smaller wire representation via base91, and richer preview data (alpha, aspect ratio, full DCT). ThumbHash is strictly superior on every axis — making this a clear win for the protocol.

For an in-depth, 1:1 comparison of BlurHash and ThumbHash fidelity, please visit https://evanw.github.io/thumbhash/

### Changes

- IMETA tags now emit `thumbhash <base91>` instead of `blurhash <base83>`
- All `blurhash` fields renamed to `thumbhash` across `ImageMetadata`, `MediaMetadata`, `EncryptedMediaUpload`, `GroupImageUpload`, and `MediaProcessingOptions`
- Old IMETA tags with `blurhash` fields are silently ignored during parsing

## Performance

Benchmarked on Apple M-series, 100x75 RGBA input:

| Operation | `blurhash` | `fast-thumbhash` | Speedup |
|-----------|------------|-------------------|---------|
| Encode    | ~180 µs    | 14.4 µs           | **12x** |
| Decode    | 18.3 µs    | 1.5 µs            | **12x** |

## Wire efficiency

| | BlurHash (base83) | fast-thumbhash (base91) |
|---|---|---|
| **Typical string size** | 28 chars | **26 chars** |
| **Alpha channel** | No | Yes |
| **Aspect ratio** | No | Embedded |
| **Detail** | 4x3 RGB grid | Full DCT L/P/Q/A |

### Nostr data savings at scale

Over **10,000 images** sent on Nostr:

- BlurHash: 28 chars × 10k = **280 KB** of placeholder data
- ThumbHash (base91): 26 chars × 10k = **260 KB** of placeholder data
- **7.1% reduction** (20 KB saved) — while encoding strictly *more* information per hash (alpha, aspect ratio, full DCT channels)

This compounds across relays that store and replicate events. Every relay serving these events benefits from the smaller payload, and every client decoding them benefits from the 12x faster decode.

- [x] All 336 unit tests pass
- [x] Tested end-to-end in Vector (macOS → Android, encode + decode)

title: fix: tighten minimum encrypted content length check from 12 to 28 bytes
body:
## Summary

Fixes an incorrect minimum-length guard in `decrypt_message_with_exporter_secret`.

## Background

The decoded `event.content` has the format:

```
base64(nonce || ciphertext)
```

where:
- `nonce` = 12 bytes (random)
- `ciphertext` = ChaCha20-Poly1305 output = `encrypted_plaintext || 16-byte Poly1305 tag`

ChaCha20 is a stream cipher so `len(ciphertext) == len(plaintext) + 16`. The Poly1305 tag is always present, even for zero-length plaintext. Therefore the minimum valid decoded length is:

> **12 (nonce) + 16 (Poly1305 tag) + 0 (empty plaintext) = 28 bytes**

## Problem

The previous guard was:

```rust
if combined.len() < 12 { ... }
```

This only rejected buffers too short to extract the nonce. Inputs in the 12–27 byte range would pass the guard and be handed to ChaCha20-Poly1305's `decrypt()` with a structurally impossible ciphertext (fewer than 16 bytes, so no valid Poly1305 tag can exist). The AEAD layer would ultimately reject them, but the early-exit check was semantically wrong and the error message misleading.

This was surfaced as feedback on the Marmot protocol spec PR [marmot-protocol/marmot#48](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/marmot/pull/48), which had the same 12-byte figure in its spec text.

## Changes

- Added `MIN_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_LEN = 28` constant with explanatory comment
- Changed the guard to `combined.len() < MIN_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_LEN`
- Updated the error message to describe the 28-byte minimum correctly
- Updated the doc comment on the function to document the minimum
- Renamed `test_decrypt_rejects_short_nonce` → `test_decrypt_rejects_too_short_content` and extended it to cover lengths `[0, 1, 11, 12, 13, 27]`, explicitly testing the previously-unchecked 12–27 window


<!-- This is an auto-generated comment: release notes by coderabbit.ai -->

⚠️ Security-sensitive changes

This PR fixes an incorrect length validation in the message decryption function that was allowing cryptographically invalid ciphertexts to be processed. The minimum encrypted content length check is tightened from 12 bytes to 28 bytes to properly account for the 12-byte nonce plus the mandatory 16-byte Poly1305 authentication tag. This prevents structurally malformed ciphertexts from reaching the AEAD layer with impossible parameters, improving error clarity and security.

**What changed:**
- Introduces `MIN_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_LEN` constant (28 bytes) with documentation explaining it represents nonce (12 bytes) + Poly1305 tag (16 bytes) + minimum plaintext (0 bytes), affecting mdk-core.
- Updates the length guard in `decrypt_message_with_exporter_secret` from `combined.len() < 12` to `combined.len() < MIN_ENCRYPTED_CONTENT_LEN`.
- Updates the error message to reflect the new 28-byte minimum requirement.
- Renames and expands the test from `test_decrypt_rejects_short_nonce` to `test_decrypt_rejects_too_short_content`, covering decoded lengths 0, 1, 11, 12, 13, and 27 bytes to explicitly exercise the previously-unguarded 12–27 byte range.
- Updates changelog with the fix under the Unreleased section with reference to PR #230.

**Security impact:**
- Tightens cryptographic validation in the ChaCha20-Poly1305 AEAD decryption path by rejecting structurally invalid ciphertexts before they reach the cipher implementation.
- Prevents edge cases where ciphertexts with impossible lengths (12–27 bytes) could produce misleading errors instead of clear rejection.

**Testing:**

## Summary

Implements the breaking changes from [marmot-protocol/marmot#48](https://github.com/marmot-protocol/marmot/pull/48):

- **MIP-03**: Replace NIP-44 encryption with direct ChaCha20-Poly1305 for kind:445 Group Message Events
- **MIP-04**: Update MLS exporter label from `("nostr", "nostr")` to `("marmot", "encrypted-media")`

## Changes

### MIP-03: ChaCha20-Poly1305 for kind:445

- **Encryption key**: `MLS-Exporter("marmot", "group-event", 32)`
- **Content format**: `base64(nonce || ciphertext)` where nonce is 12 random bytes and ciphertext includes the 16-byte Poly1305 tag
- **AAD**: none (MIP-03 path now encrypts without AAD)
- **Nonce**: cryptographically random via `OsRng` per message; RNG failure aborts encryption
- Removed NIP-44 dependency from `mdk-core`; added `base64` as a direct workspace dependency

### MIP-04: Updated exporter label

- `mip04_exporter_secret()` now uses `MLS-Exporter("marmot", "encrypted-media", 32)` separately from the MIP-03 exporter
- MIP-04 exporter secrets are stored separately from MIP-03 secrets and persisted per epoch for media decryption lookback

### Storage and migration updates

- SQLite migration `V005` now rebuilds `group_exporter_secrets` with `PRIMARY KEY (mls_group_id, epoch, label)`
- Existing rows are migrated as `label = 'group-event'`
- Snapshot/rollback logic now preserves exporter `label`, with backward-compatible restore support for legacy unlabeled snapshot keys
- Added GroupStorage MIP-04 methods and backend implementations:
  - `get_group_mip04_exporter_secret`
  - `save_group_mip04_exporter_secret`

### Correctness and hardening follow-ups in this PR

- Persist MIP-04 exporter secrets when processing incoming commits (not only self-commits)
- Redact MIP-04 storage save errors in `process.rs` to avoid leaking raw backend error text
- Added label-isolation tests (MIP-03 vs MIP-04) across shared, sqlite, memory, and cross-backend suites
- Added integration test covering media decrypt after incoming-commit epoch advancement
- Added snapshot isolation coverage for MIP-04 exporter secrets in memory storage

## Breaking changes

- kind:445 content format is incompatible with prior NIP-44 versions
- MIP-04 encrypted media produced with old exporter labels cannot be decrypted with this version
- SQLite storage schema change requires migration

- `just precommit` passes
- Added targeted regression tests for:
  - label-aware exporter storage and isolation
  - incoming-commit MIP-04 secret persistence
  - legacy unlabeled snapshot key restore fallback
  - cross-epoch media decryption with incoming-commit advancement

title: fix: wire max_past_epochs into OpenMLS group config and bump to 0.8.1
body:
## Summary

- **Bug fix**: MDK was not setting `max_past_epochs` on the OpenMLS group config (defaulted to 0). Application messages from epoch N that arrived after a commit advanced the group to epoch N+1 were permanently marked `Failed` with `SecretTreeError::TooDistantInThePast`. This is a real-world failure on Nostr relays where delivery ordering is not guaranteed.
- **Fix**: Added `max_past_epochs: usize` (default 5) to `MdkConfig` and wired it into both `MlsGroupCreateConfig` (group creation) and `MlsGroupJoinConfig` (welcome join). Exposed through the `mdk-uniffi` `MdkConfig` record as `max_past_epochs: Option<u32>`.
- **Dependency bump**: `openmls` 0.8.0 → 0.8.1 (security fix for authenticated tag comparison, [GHSA-8x3w-qj7j-gqhf](https://github.com/openmls/openmls/security/advisories/GHSA-8x3w-qj7j-gqhf)) and `openmls_rust_crypto` 0.5.0 → 0.5.1.

## Regression tests

Two concrete tests prove the bug and verify the fix:

- `test_past_epoch_application_message_fails_without_max_past_epochs`: Alice sends at epoch 1, group advances to epoch 2 via self-update commit, Bob receives the delayed message → `Unprocessable` (bug confirmed with `max_past_epochs = 0`)
- `test_past_epoch_application_message_succeeds_with_max_past_epochs`: Same scenario with `max_past_epochs = 5` → `ApplicationMessage` with correct content decrypted (fix verified)

## Impact

Any group member who receives an application message after a commit has already advanced the group epoch will now successfully decrypt that message (within the 5-epoch window), rather than having it permanently lost. This affects all commit types — self-updates, member adds, member removes — not just join self-updates.
